title: Index Laws: Multiplying, Dividing, Power of a Power and the Zero Exponent

key_big: Same base: multiply → add the exponents, divide → subtract, power of a power → multiply.
key_sub: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.
body_html:
How it works

The exponent (index) tells you how many times the base is multiplied by itself. With the same base:

  • Multiplying: add the exponents. 23 × 24 = 27
  • Dividing: subtract the exponents. 56 ÷ 52 = 54
  • Power of a power: multiply the exponents. (32)4 = 38
  • Zero exponent: any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1. 70 = 1
Example

Simplify 45 × 43.

Same base: add 5 + 3.

Answer: 48

Example

Work out 107 ÷ 104.

Subtract: 103.

Answer: 1000

Example

Simplify (23)2.

Multiply 3 × 2.

Answer: 26 = 64

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying the exponents when you multiply powers: 23 × 24 = 27, not 212.
  • Multiplying the bases: 34 × 32 = 36, not 96.
  • Thinking 50 = 0. It is 1.
  • Adding the exponents for a power of a power: (32)4 = 38, not 36.

faq.a: With the same base, add exponents when multiplying, subtract when dividing, and multiply when raising a power to a power. Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

faq.q: Why is any number to the power 0 equal to 1?
faq.a: Because aⁿ ÷ aⁿ = a⁰, and any number divided by itself is 1.

faq.q: Can I use index laws with different bases?
faq.a: Not directly. 2³ × 3² cannot be written as one power, but 4³ can be rewritten as 2⁶ first.

faq.q: What is the difference between 2³ × 2⁴ and (2³)⁴?
